summary_oneline: Make the packaged SDD flow work in non-Python repositories: config out of pyproject.toml, reachable test runners, auto-detected toolchain profiles, worktree setup, language-neutral prompts

the loader every new consumer goes through
reads [tool.parrot.sdd] sandbox from pyproject.toml only
reads sandbox_allowed_domains / gh_token from the primary checkout's pyproject.toml only
per-launch flags, the only alternative today
reads [tool.parrot.worktree] from pyproject.toml only
the manifest model to reuse unchanged under the new home
the only writer of [tool.parrot.sdd]
the post-create hook point: native sync today, setup command tomorrow
git-ignores all of .parrot/, including the runner settings file
runner registry and its .parrot/test_runners.toml config path
vitest adapter: mandatory TOML cwd, pnpm-only, admin-ui default
feeds TOML settings to non-pytest adapters
rewrite target that only exists in the ai-parrot monorepo
--run path ignores invocation.cwd and appends a pytest flag
engine lint pass: formatter detection from pyproject.toml
engine lint pass: .py-only file filter
tool audit lists black/pylint regardless of the repository
unconditional ruff + mypy gate
Python-only probe commands
full lint pass, ruff-only
lint/type-check step, ruff/mypy-only (guarded)
format hook, .py + black/pylint only

pytest-only validation guidance

constraints.statement: Security-sensitive settings are read from the PRIMARY checkout only, and sandbox modes off/legacy are never settable from a file
constraints.implication: the sdd/config.json reader for sandbox policy, runner settings and the worktree setup command must resolve the primary checkout, not the worktree copy; a command that runs on the host must never come from a branch the sandboxed session can write

constraints.statement: SddConfig uses extra=forbid and ensure_worktree loads native_artifacts.py by file path with stdlib + pydantic only
constraints.implication: new keys are a model change (older parrot versions reject a config that carries them), and the shared reader must stay importable without importing the parrot package

constraints.statement: ai-parrot itself declares both tables in pyproject.toml and tracks .parrot/test_runners.toml
constraints.implication: pyproject.toml and the TOML file stay as fallbacks; ai-parrot needs no migration to keep working

constraints.statement: .parrot/ is git-ignored in target repositories and becomes the worktree root under FEAT-802
constraints.implication: committed configuration cannot live under .parrot/; runner settings need a committed home

constraints.statement: A sandboxed session cannot reach a package registry or write a user-level package store
constraints.implication: dependency setup has to run on the host at worktree creation, before the sandboxed session starts

constraints.statement: Formatting and auto-fixable lint are engine-owned by design, not coder-turn work
constraints.implication: a toolchain profile must plug into the engine lint pass, not only into prompt text

constraints.statement: FEAT-802 and FEAT-804 are approved and touch the installer, the worktree root and the install-root resolver
constraints.implication: this work sequences after them; the installer and ensure_worktree edits must be rebased on their result

constraints.statement: Every shipped prompt has host twins (claude, agent, agents, codex)
constraints.implication: each prompt change lands in all copies and is covered by the existing asset-sync checks

new.name: Repository settings in sdd/config.json

new.name: Toolchain profile detection
new.role: one module that maps marker files (pyproject.toml, package.json, Cargo.toml) to the format / lint / type-check / test commands and file suffixes of a repository, exposed to scripts and, through one CLI verb, to prompts

new.name: Worktree setup command
new.role: a declared command ensure_worktree runs on the host after creating a worktree

new.name: Foreign-repository end-to-end fixture
new.role: a minimal Node + vitest repository exercised from install to select_tests, guard and worktree creation

risks.statement: A config written by a newer parrot is rejected by an older one (extra=forbid)
A host-side setup command is arbitrary code execution if it is read from an untrusted ref
Auto-detection is ambiguous in mixed-language repositories; ai-parrot itself is Python plus a Svelte UI
The reference repository has a live worktree under .claude/worktrees, which FEAT-802 makes the installer refuse
The prompt inventory beyond the spot-checked lines is second-hand

unknowns.question: Where must the configuration that today lives only in pyproject.toml live for a repository without one?
plausible_answers: b) parrot.toml at the repository root
unknowns.user_answer: sdd/config.json (extend SddConfig; pyproject.toml stays as a fallback)

unknowns.question: What scope should the proposal cover?
unknowns.user_answer: Everything, in phases: config and runners; lint/format and worktree dependencies; neutral prompts, templates and contract-probe; migrate navigator-frontend-next as the acceptance test

unknowns.question: How does a non-Python repository declare lint, format and type-check?
unknowns.user_answer: Auto-detected profiles (detect package.json, Cargo.toml, ... and pick the tools)

unknowns.question: How does a new worktree get its dependencies?
plausible_answers: a) a declared setup command run by ensure_worktree on the host
b) a link to the main checkout's node_modules
unknowns.user_answer: A declared setup command that ensure_worktree runs on the host when it creates the worktree

unknowns.question: Open design choices left for the spec: (1) runner settings as a block in sdd/config.json or an un-ignored .parrot/test_runners.toml; (2) contract probe as an extension-keyed command table or wikitoolkit symbols; (3) whether a detected profile can be overridden or scoped by path in sdd/config.json; (4) when the setup command re-runs and whether its failure blocks

recommended_next_command.rationale: localization is high-confidence for phases 1 and 2 and the four scope decisions are taken; the remaining choices are bounded and belong to the spec's own Q&A. The spec should cut the phases into separately shippable features.

meta.notes: overall_confidence is medium, not high: the prompt inventory (C15) is partly second-hand, C8 was not executed, and C19 is untested. Research ran before the skill was invoked and was not budget-metered; consumed counters are estimates.
